docs.title: Inim SmartLiving Alarm for Home Assistant
docs.text:
This integration connects Home Assistant to an Inim SmartLiving alarm panel on your local network. You can see the state of every area and zone, arm and disarm, run the panel's scenarios and switch its outputs, from dashboards and automations.

Not an official Inim product

This integration is not made or supported by Inim Electronics. Use it at your own risk.

The SmartLiving 1050 on firmware 6 is tested and confirmed by several users. The SmartLiving 10100 with a SmartLAN/G board is confirmed by one user. The SmartLiving 505 and 515, and all four models on firmware 5.1, are supported experimentally. Reports from users of these panels help.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
1. Check the requirements: a supported panel, a SmartLAN/SI or SmartLAN/G board on your network, and a user code (PIN) of the panel.
  2. Install the integration and restart Home Assistant.
  3. Add your panel: enter the board's address and the PIN, then choose what to import.
  4. Find your entities on the panel's device page, and add them to a dashboard.

Coming from version 0.3? Read Upgrading first. Something not working? See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
Part of the panel What you can do Page The whole panel Arm and disarm with the alarm panel card, using the panel's scenarios Entities Each area Arm or disarm it, choose the arming mode, see alarm, tamper and alarm memory Entities Each zone See whether it is open, in tamper or has an alarm memory; bypass it Entities Each scenario Run it with a button; see whether it is active Entities Outputs Switch lights, gates and other outputs; dim dimmers Entities Event log See the panel's recent events, with names Entities Automations Arm areas, run scenarios and reset the alarm memory with actions; react to events Actions and events

Before arming an area or running a scenario, the integration asks the panel which zones are not ready, and refuses or arms anyway with a warning, as you choose (see Zones not ready).

docs.title: Words used on this site
docs.text: Word Meaning Panel The SmartLiving alarm control unit (central unit). SmartLAN board The network board in the panel: SmartLAN/SI or SmartLAN/G. Home Assistant talks to the panel through it. Area A part of the house that is armed and disarmed together, for example Ground floor. Other systems call it a partition. Zone One detector input: a door contact, a motion sensor, a smoke detector. Each zone belongs to one or more areas. Terminal A connection on the panel or on an expander. A terminal is programmed as an input (one zone), an output, or both. Double terminal and second zone A terminal programmed with two zones on the same wires. Its second zone has a number above the panel's terminals: 51 to 100 on the SmartLiving 1050, for example. Scenario A set of actions programmed on the panel, for example Night: arm some areas, disarm others. Output A terminal or one of the fixed outputs O1 to O3 that drives something: a light, a gate, a siren. Home automation output An output the installer marked for home automation in the panel's programming. Only these are ticked for you at setup. Alarm memory After an alarm, the panel remembers which areas and zones raised it, until the memory is reset. Bypass Excluding a zone, so it cannot raise an alarm until it is included again. User code and PIN A user code is a user programmed on the panel (for example Master). Its PIN is the number typed to use it. Home Assistant sends commands with one PIN, so it can control only the areas of that user code. Programming mode While someone programs the panel from a keypad, it ignores commands. No command is sent then.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome: open an issue or a pull request on GitHub.

docs.title: Actions and events
docs.text: This page shows how to arm, disarm and run scenarios from dashboards and automations, and how automations can react to the integration's events. The reference at the end lists every field.

docs.title: From a dashboard
docs.text:
• The whole panel: add the alarm panel entity to Home Assistant's alarm panel card. Its buttons run the scenarios you mapped in the options.

  • One area: add the area's switch (on arms, off disarms) or its arming mode select (choose the mode). A tile card with the select's options feature shows the modes as a list:

  • A scenario: add its button.

  • An output: add its switch or light (see Outputs).

docs.title: Arming areas from automations
docs.text:
Use the Arm area action to arm or disarm one or more areas of a panel in a single command, so they change together. In the automation editor, add the action Arm area, pick the panel, tick the areas and choose the mode:

In YAML, areas are the area numbers as on the panel:

action: inim_smartliving_alarm.arm_area
data:
  config_entry_id: your_config_entry_id
  areas: [1, 3]
  mode: partial

To run a scenario from an automation, use Activate scenario (see below). You can try any action from Settings → Tools → Actions (on versions before 2026.11, Developer tools → Actions).

docs.title: Resetting the alarm memory
docs.text:
After an alarm, the panel keeps the alarm memory of the areas involved until it is reset; the Area N Alarm memory sensors show it. The Alarm Reset action resets every area of the panel that has an alarm or tamper memory:

action: inim_smartliving_alarm.alarm_reset
target:
  entity_id: alarm_control_panel.your_panel_name

You can call it from a script, an automation or a dashboard button.

docs.title: Zones not ready
docs.text:
Before it arms an area or runs a scenario, the integration asks the panel which zones are not ready: zones that are not at rest and would be armed. Then the option When zones are not ready (in General settings) decides:

  • Refuse (the default): nothing is sent. You get an error that lists the zones, for example "Area 3 was not armed because these zones are not ready: Kitchen window (12)".

  • Arm anyway and warn: the command is sent, and a notification lists the zones. They can set off an alarm unless they are closed or bypassed in time.

force: true on the Arm area and Activate scenario actions arms anyway for that call, whatever the option says. Disarming is never checked. Either way, the inim_smartliving_alarm_zones_not_ready event fires, for example to announce the open zones.

Which commands are checked, and the panel's own rule
  • Checked: the area switch, the arming mode select and Arm area (arming an area), and the scenario button, the alarm panel and Activate scenario (running a scenario).
  • Zones the panel bypasses by itself when arming (autobypassable zones) are not listed.
  • The installer can also set the panel itself not to allow arming with zones not ready. The integration reads that setting with the panel configuration and shows it in the Refuses arming with zones not ready sensor (and as panel_refuses_not_ready in the event). When it is on, the panel refuses such a command even when you arm anyway or use force: the integration still sends it, the message says the panel refused it, and the event's action is refused_by_panel.
  • The panel's own rule depends on each zone's programming (for example, delayed zones do not stop total arming, and zones with no_arming_if_not_ready stop every mode), so it may let through zones the integration lists. When the setting is off, the panel arms whatever the zones' programming says.

docs.title: The event log on a dashboard
docs.text:
A Markdown card shows the last events of the event log sensor. Replace sensor.home_home_event_log with your event log sensor's ID:

type: markdown
title: Alarm events
content: >-
  {% for e in (state_attr('sensor.home_home_event_log', 'event_log') or [])[:10] %}
  - {{ as_timestamp(e.timestamp) | timestamp_custom('%d/%m %H:%M') }}
  · {{ e.description }}{% if e.authorized_by %} · {{ e.authorized_by }}{% endif %}{% if e.affected_areas %} · {{ e.affected_areas }}{% endif %}
  {% endfor %}

The repository's Examples folder has a larger dashboard, made for version 0.3: its entity IDs and some cards may need changes.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: None of the actions returns a response. If a command is not carried out, the action fails with a message that says why (see When the panel refuses a command).

docs.title: Arm area
docs.text:
inim_smartliving_alarm.arm_area: arms or disarms one or more areas of a panel in a single command. Before arming, it checks the zones (see Zones not ready).

Field Required Type and values Default Example config_entry_id yes the panel (a list of your panels in the editor) – 01J… areas yes a list of area numbers, as on the panel; the editor lists the imported areas by name – [1, 3] mode yes total, partial, instant, disarm – partial force no true arms even if zones are not ready false true When it fails
  • With several panels, the editor shows each area number with the name it has on every panel that imports it; the panel you pick decides which one is armed.
  • An area that is not imported from that panel (for example, one you unticked after writing the automation) is refused with a message, and nothing is sent.
  • It also fails when the panel is not found or not loaded, when zones are not ready and the option says Refuse, and when the panel refuses the command.

docs.title: Activate scenario
docs.text:
inim_smartliving_alarm.activate_scenario: runs a scenario of the panel. Before running it, it checks the zones (see Zones not ready).

Field Required Type and values Default Example config_entry_id yes the panel – 01J… scenario yes the scenario number, as on the panel (from 1); the editor lists the imported scenarios by name – 2 force no true runs it even if zones are not ready false true 
action: inim_smartliving_alarm.activate_scenario
data:
  config_entry_id: your_config_entry_id
  scenario: 2

A scenario that is not imported from that panel is refused with a message. A failed activation also shows a notification and fires the inim_smartliving_alarm_scenario_activation_failed event.

docs.title: Alarm Reset
docs.text:
inim_smartliving_alarm.alarm_reset: resets the alarm and tamper memory of every area of the panel that has one.

Field Required Type and values Default Example target entity_id yes the panel's alarm panel entity – alarm_control_panel.home

Entities of other integrations in the target are skipped. If the panel's integration is not loaded, the action fails with a message.

docs.title: Re-read panel configuration
docs.text:
inim_smartliving_alarm.reread_panel_configuration: reads the panel configuration again and reloads the integration, like the button of the same name (see Setup).

Field Required Type and values Default Example config_entry_id yes the panel – 01J… 
action: inim_smartliving_alarm.reread_panel_configuration
data:
  config_entry_id: your_config_entry_id

It fails, and keeps the stored configuration, when the panel cannot be reached, is in programming mode, or returns an incomplete configuration.

docs.title: Events
docs.text: Automations can react to these events with an event trigger.

docs.title: Zones not ready
docs.text:
inim_smartliving_alarm_zones_not_ready fires each time an area is armed or a scenario is run with zones not ready, whether the command was refused or sent anyway.

Field Values config_entry_id the panel's configuration entry target the area's name, several area names separated by commas (from Arm area), or the scenario's name action refused (not sent), armed_anyway (sent with a warning), refused_by_panel (sent, and the panel refused it) zones the zones not ready, each with zone_id (the number) and zone_name (for example Kitchen window (12)) panel_refuses_not_ready true or false: whether the panel itself refuses arming with zones not ready; null before the configuration was read again by this version 
triggers:
  - trigger: event
    event_type: inim_smartliving_alarm_zones_not_ready

docs.title: Scenario activation failed
docs.text:
inim_smartliving_alarm_scenario_activation_failed fires each time a scenario cannot be run: from the alarm panel, a scenario button or Activate scenario. A scenario refused because zones are not ready fires both events.

Field Values entity_unique_id the unique ID of the entity that ran it entity_name the name of that entity action what was asked, in English, for example arm away or activate scenario 'Night' scenario_index the scenario number minus 1 scenario_name the scenario's name reason zones_blocked, no_areas_identified, unknown_zones_error, no_data_available, disarm_failed, panel_programming, command_failed, unknown, or the reason the panel gave (see below) panel_result the panel's reason when it refused the command, unknown for a reason the integration does not know, or null when the panel did not refuse it blocking_zones the zones that stopped it, each with zone_id, zone_name, status (not_ready, alarmed, short or tamper) and areas (by name) message a description, always in English, whatever Home Assistant's language

The panel's reasons are invalid_code, open_zones, code_not_enabled, already_in_state, slot_out_of_range, slot_not_connected, null_terminal, cannot_be_bypassed, no_areas, double_zone_error, output_not_enabled, areas_armed and refused; what each means is on Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Switching outputs
docs.text: See Outputs.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text: Your panel appears in Home Assistant as one device, named as you chose at setup. Its entities are the areas, zones, scenarios and outputs you import, plus a few sensors about the panel itself. Open the device page from Settings → Devices & services → Inim SmartLiving Alarm.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
Part Entities What you do with them The panel an alarm panel Arm and disarm with the alarm panel card, using your scenarios Each area a switch, an arming mode select, three binary sensors Arm or disarm the area; see alarm, tamper and alarm memory Each zone a binary sensor, a switch, two more binary sensors See whether the zone is open; bypass it; see tamper and alarm memory Each scenario a button, a binary sensor Run the scenario; see whether it is active Each output a switch, or a light for dimmers Switch or dim the output The panel's state sensors The event log, the active scenario, firmware and model Diagnostics sensors, a select, a button The user code, the devices found, programming mode, system reports, re-reading the configuration

For example, the tile cards of an area: its arming mode, its switch and its alarm memory.

Entity IDs

Entity IDs start with your panel's name: with the name Home, area 1's switch is switch.home_home_area_1 on a new installation (the name appears twice, see Known limitations), or switch.home_area_1 on one set up with an earlier version. The tables below give the end of each ID; N is the area, zone or scenario number. Every entity is enabled by default, except Diagnostics level.

docs.title: The alarm panel
docs.text:
ID ends with Name States alarm_control_panel.… the panel's name armed home, armed away, armed night, armed vacation, armed custom bypass, disarmed, triggered

The alarm panel arms and disarms with the scenarios you mapped in the options. Use it with Home Assistant's alarm panel card. No code is asked.

How the state is worked out
  • Triggered while any area is in alarm.
  • Otherwise the mode whose scenario is active on the panel, for example Armed night.
  • A scenario active on the panel that is not mapped to a mode shows as Armed custom bypass.
  • Without a mapped Disarm scenario, the state is unknown when no mapping matches.
  • Only the arm modes with a mapped scenario are offered. Disarming or arming without a mapped scenario fails with a message ("No scenario is mapped to … choose one in the integration options").

docs.title: Areas
docs.text:
ID ends with Name States Device class switch.…_area_N panel Area N (name) on when armed in any mode – select.…_area_N_arming_mode Area N arming mode Disarmed, Armed total, Armed partial, Armed instant – binary_sensor.…_area_N_alarm Area N Alarm (name) on while the area is in alarm safety binary_sensor.…_area_N_tamper Area N Tamper (name) on while the area is in tamper tamper binary_sensor.…_area_N_triggered Area N Alarm memory (name) on after an alarm, until the memory is reset safety
  • The switch arms the area when you turn it on and disarms it when you turn it off. It arms in the area's own mode set under Area switches arm mode per area, else in Area switches default arm mode (total by default).
  • The arming mode select arms the area in the mode you choose, or disarms it. If the panel refuses, an error says why. It is unknown while the panel reports none of the four modes.
  • The alarm memory stays on after an alarm until it is reset (see Resetting the alarm memory). Home Assistant shows the safety class as Unsafe while it is on.

Arming from the switch or the select checks the zones first: see Zones not ready.

Attributes of the area entities Attribute On Values area_id all area entities the area's number area_name all area entities the area's name on the panel status_text switch armed, disarmed, unknown; Unknown when the panel reports no state for the area arming_mode switch total, partial, instant, disarmed, unknown tamper_memory alarm memory true when the area also has a tamper memory exit_time arming mode select time to leave after arming, for example 120 s or 2 min entry_time arming mode select time to disarm after a delayed zone opens entry_time_2 arming mode select the second entry time, used by zones with the entry_time_2 option, or not used pre_arm_warning_time arming mode select in minutes, for example 3 min patrol_time arming mode select in minutes timer_program arming mode select the arm/disarm timer program, or none reset_alarm_memory_on_arming arming mode select true or false auto_arm_partial arming mode select true or false clear_call_queue_on_disarm arming mode select true or false

The switch shows status_text and arming_mode once the panel's state has been read. The select's delays and options are as programmed on the panel; they are not shown for panels handled with another model's layout (see Known limitations).

docs.title: Zones
docs.text:
Only zones that exist on the panel get entities: zones of input, input/output and double terminals. Output terminals (for example a siren) and unused terminals have none. Zones 1 to N are the zones of the panel's N terminals (50 on the SmartLiving 1050, 100 on the 10100); a double terminal n also has a second zone, numbered N + n (51 to 100 on the 1050, 101 to 200 on the 10100).

ID ends with Name States Device class binary_sensor.…_zone_N Zone N (name) on while the zone is in alarm (open) guessed, see below binary_sensor.…_zone_N_triggered Zone N Alarm memory (name) on after the zone raised an alarm, until the memory is reset problem binary_sensor.…_zone_N_tamper Zone N Tamper (name) on while the zone is in tamper or short circuit tamper switch.…_zone_N panel Zone N Enabled (name) on: included; off: bypassed –
  • The zone sensor is on while the zone is open or in alarm. A short circuit or tamper shows in its status_text and in the zone's tamper sensor.
  • The zone switch bypasses the zone when you turn it off, and includes it again when you turn it on.
Device class of the zone sensor

A wired zone does not tell the panel what detector it has, so the device class is a guess from the zone's programming:

Zone programming Device class shock sensor vibration roller-blind sensor, normally open or normally closed contact, single EOL balancing opening double EOL balancing motion anything else none

If the guess is wrong, change it in Home Assistant: open the entity's settings and pick Show as.

The zone sensor's attributes are the zone's programming, as read from the panel. Open the sensor, then the menu (⋮) → Details:

Attributes of the zone entities Attribute On Values zone_id all zone entities the zone's number zone_name all zone entities the zone's name on the panel status_text sensor, tamper clear, alarmed, short, tamper; Unknown when the panel reports no state test sensor true while the zone is in test internal_index sensor, switch the zone's position in the panel's status (0-based) tamper_memory alarm memory true when the zone's terminal has a tamper memory (both zones of a double terminal share it) zone_type sensor instant, delayed, viewable_delayed, route, 24_hour, automation, arm, disarm, switch, arm_disarm, patrol, emergency_exit_without_call, emergency_exit; a number for a value not listed here assigned_areas sensor the numbers of the zone's areas alarm_cycles sensor how many times the zone can raise an alarm, or unlimited sensor_kind sensor generic, roller_blind, shock alarm_pulse_duration sensor generic sensors only: for example 300 ms or 20 s (the panel counts in steps of 15 ms or of 10 s) shock_sensitivity sensor shock sensors only: 0 to 40 pulse_window_time sensor the time in which pulses are counted, for example 30 s or 1 min pulse_count sensor how many pulses in that time raise the alarm balancing sensor normally_open, normally_closed, single_eol, double_eol, double_zone, double_zone_eol, personalized terminal_index sensor the zone's terminal (0-based) terminal_type sensor input, output, in_out, double, null, out_dimming, out_dac, out_analog, out_not_enabled second_zone sensor true for the second zone of a double terminal interior sensor true or false autobypass sensor bypassed by the panel when its areas arm while it is open unbypassable sensor true or false chime sensor true or false test_programmed sensor true or false autobypass_no_reinclude sensor autobypassed and not included again when back at rest no_arming_if_not_ready sensor stops arming in every mode, when the panel refuses arming with zones not ready entry_time_2 sensor uses the area's second entry time last_exit_zone sensor true or false reinclude_on_disarm sensor true or false hold_up sensor true or false fault_zone sensor true or false

The programming attributes (from zone_type on) are not shown when the panel data stored for the zone cannot be read; use Re-read panel configuration then. Options that only apply to wireless zones are not shown.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
ID ends with Name States button.…_scenario_N Activate 'name' – binary_sensor.…_scenario_N_active Scenario 'name' Active on while the scenario is the active one on the panel
  • The button runs the scenario. If it fails (a zone not ready, or the panel refuses), an error and a persistent notification give the reason.
  • For scenarios, N is the scenario number minus 1: scenario 1 is scenario_0. Area and zone numbers, and the scenario field of the activate_scenario action, start from 1.
Attributes of the scenario entities Attribute On Values scenario_index button, binary sensor the scenario number minus 1 scenario_name button, binary sensor the scenario's name on the panel area_actions_details button what the scenario does to each area, by area number: keep, total, partial, instant, disarm, unknown

docs.title: Sensors
docs.text:
ID ends with Name State sensor.…_event_log panel Event Log the position of the newest event in the panel's log sensor.…_active_scenario Active Scenario Name the active scenario's name and index, for example Night (Index 1) sensor.…_firmware_version Firmware Version the panel's firmware, for example 6.07 sensor.…_system_type System Type the panel's model, for example 01050
  • The event log keeps the recent events, with the names programmed on the panel: who did it and where. It keeps its last events while the panel cannot be reached. To show it on a dashboard, see The event log on a dashboard.
  • The firmware and system type sensors are created when the panel reports them.
The event log in detail

The state is the position of the newest event in the panel's event log: 0 to 999, or 0 to 499 on panels that keep 500 events (the SmartLiving 505 and 515, and the 1050 on firmware 5.1). It starts again from 0 when the log wraps around, so it changes with every new event. Before the first read it is Unknown Index.

Attribute Values event_log the recent events, newest first (see below) event_log_count_current how many events are in event_log now event_log_size_configured the Number of Events to store in log option latest_event_description the newest event's description latest_event_timestamp the newest event's time

Each event in event_log has:

Key Values timestamp the event's time: the panel's clock read in Home Assistant's time zone, with daylight saving time description what happened, for example Area(s) Armed authorized_by the user code or key that did it, by name device the keypad or reader, by name; Remote for commands from the app, the cloud, Home Assistant or the installer software affected_areas the areas, by name area the area, for events about one area zone the zone, for zone events scenario the scenario, for scenario events authorized_id, device_id the numbers of the user code or key, and of the keypad or reader (hexadecimal) raw_hex_data the event as stored by the panel

Keys that do not apply to an event are left out.

The active scenario in detail

The state is the active scenario's name followed by its index (0-based). It is Unknown Scenario (Index n) for an index without a scenario name, and Unknown (No data) or Unknown (No active index) when the panel reports none.

Attribute Values active_scenario_index the index alone raw_active_scenario_hex the panel's raw value

docs.title: Diagnostic and configuration entities
docs.text:
These are shown in the Diagnostic and Configuration sections of the device page.

ID ends with Name State button.…_reread_panel_configuration Re-read panel configuration reads the panel configuration again and reloads (see Setup) sensor.…_user_code User code the name of the user code the PIN belongs to (never the PIN) sensor.…_peripherals Peripherals how many keypads, readers, expanders and sirens are enabled binary_sensor.…_programming_mode Programming mode on while the panel is in programming mode binary_sensor.…_refuses_arming_with_zones_not_ready Refuses arming with zones not ready on when the installer set the panel to refuse arming with zones not ready select.…_diagnostics_level Diagnostics level Redacted, Full, Full confidential; disabled by default Details and attributes
  • User code: commands only work on the areas of this user code. Unknown if the PIN matches no user code: commands are refused then. Checked again whenever the integration reloads.
  • Peripherals: it does not tell whether a device is answering.
  • Programming mode: on while the panel is being programmed from a keypad, or reloading its configuration. Commands are not sent then. It is unavailable for panels handled with the SmartLiving 1050's layout (other models, firmware 5.0x).
  • Refuses arming with zones not ready: read with the panel configuration; unknown until the configuration is read again by this version. See Zones not ready.
  • Diagnostics level: how much the next diagnostics download shows (see System report). It goes back to Redacted when the integration restarts or reloads, after the readable copy of a Full report has been downloaded, and 10 minutes after a Full report's first download.
Attribute On Values number User code the user code's number areas User code the areas it controls, by name type User code standard, manager, master keypads, readers, expanders, sirens Peripherals the names of the enabled devices

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
Warning

An output switches whatever is wired to it: a siren, a lock, a gate, heating. Switching it from Home Assistant, or from an automation, acts on the real device. Before ticking an output, check what it drives.

ID ends with Name States switch.…_output name the output's name on the panel on while the panel shows the output active light.…_output name the output's name on the panel on or off, with brightness (dimmers)
  • On/off and monostable outputs are switches. A monostable output switches itself off after its time; the switch shows it off at the next poll.
  • Dimmers are lights with brightness. On firmware 6 the level is read from the panel at every poll and after each change; on firmware 5.1 the panel does not report it, so the brightness is the last one set from Home Assistant.
  • Outputs without a name on the panel are called Output n, or O1 to O3 for the fixed outputs.
Which outputs are offered and ticked
  • What is offered: outputs programmed on the panel as on/off, monostable or dimmer outputs (terminal outputs and O1 to O3) that your user code may switch. Analogue outputs are not offered. A terminal output on one of the panel's first three terminal positions cannot be switched remotely (the panel reserves those numbers for O1 to O3), so it is not listed.
  • What is ticked for you: only the outputs the installer marked as home automation outputs in the panel's programming (firmware 6; on firmware 5.1 the integration cannot read this mark, so nothing is ticked). The panel cannot tell what an output drives, so check them, and pick any other outputs yourself, in the setup or later in the options under Areas, zones, scenarios and outputs. The first time an existing installation shows the outputs in the options, the home automation outputs are ticked there too; after you save, your choice is kept.
  • Nothing is switched by itself: no output is switched at setup, at start, at a reload or when Home Assistant restores its state.
  • When the panel refuses: an output your user code may not switch, or one locked while its areas are armed, gives an error with the reason (see When the panel refuses a command). While the panel is in programming mode, no command is sent.
Attributes of the outputs Attribute Values output_number the output's number kind on_off, monostable, dimmer terminal_index terminal outputs: the terminal (0-based) fixed_output fixed outputs: 1 to 3 monostable_time monostable outputs: for example 30 s home_automation true if the installer marked it as a home automation output; not shown on firmware 5.1 normally_closed true or false flashing true or false buzzer true or false keep_on_restoral true or false toggle true or false relay_use true or false

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This page says what you need, and how to install the integration in Home Assistant.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
You need:

  • Home Assistant 2026.1 or later.
  • A supported Inim SmartLiving panel, on firmware 6.x or 5.1x (see the table below).
  • A SmartLAN/SI or SmartLAN/G board in the panel, connected to your network, that Home Assistant can reach.
  • The board's address and port (usually 5004). For a SmartLAN/G board, also the user name and password of the board's web page.
  • A user code (PIN) of the panel. Commands are sent with it, so it must control the areas you want to arm and disarm.

docs.title: Supported panels
docs.text:
Model Areas Zone numbers Status SmartLiving 1050 10 1-100 developed and tested on it SmartLiving 10100 15 1-200 confirmed working (SmartLAN/G) SmartLiving 515 5 1-40 experimental SmartLiving 505 5 1-20 experimental

Zone numbers above the number of terminals are the second zones of double terminals.

What experimental means, and other firmware versions
  • Experimental models use the panel's memory map but have not been tested on a real panel yet; a warning in the log says so. Please report how it works for you.
  • Firmware 6.x is supported as in the table above.

  • Firmware 5.1x is supported experimentally, and with limits, on all four models:

    • it has not been tested on a real panel on firmware 5.1;
    • the panel's state flags (such as programming mode) and the results of commands are assumed to work as on firmware 6;
    • the event log shows the free events that only firmware 5.1 has (free events 1 to 11) as unknown events;
    • video sensors are not supported (firmware 5.1 has none).

    A warning in the log says the panel's support is experimental. Please report how it works for you.

  • Firmware 5.0x and older cannot be set up ("The panel's firmware is not supported: firmware 5.1 or newer is needed").

  • Other SmartLiving models cannot be set up ("This SmartLiving model is not supported yet"); please report your model and firmware on GitHub.
SmartLAN/SI and SmartLAN/G

Both boards are supported. The SmartLAN/G board is confirmed working on a SmartLiving 10100.

docs.title: Installing
docs.text:
The integration is installed as a custom repository. Use the button to open it in your Home Assistant, or follow the steps for your version below.

Open your Home Assistant instance and open this repository in the Marketplace.

The button opens the repository in the Marketplace on Home Assistant 2026.11 or later, and in HACS on earlier versions (HACS must be installed). Download Inim Smartliving Alarm there and restart Home Assistant.

Marketplace (2026.11 or later)HACS (2026.1 to 2026.10)Manual
  1. Go to Settings → Marketplace.
  2. Add https://github.com/matteoraf/ha-inim_smartliving_alarm_panel as a custom repository of type Integration. Adding custom repositories needs the Marketplace's GitHub connection.
  3. Open Inim Smartliving Alarm in the Marketplace and install it.
  4. Restart Home Assistant.
  1. In HACS, open the menu (⋮) → Custom repositories.
  2. Add https://github.com/matteoraf/ha-inim_smartliving_alarm_panel with type Integration.
  3. Search for Inim Smartliving Alarm and download it.
  4. Restart Home Assistant.
  1. Download the inim_smartliving_alarm folder of the latest release.
  2. Copy it into your config/custom_components folder.
  3. Restart Home Assistant.

Then add your panel.

docs.title: Preview versions
docs.text:
Versions such as 0.4.0a1 (preview) or 0.4.0b1 (beta) are published as GitHub pre-releases. They are offered only to users who ask for them.

Take a backup first

Take a Home Assistant backup before installing a preview or a beta (Settings → System → Backups). A preview or a beta updates your configuration entry to a newer format that the stable 0.3.x versions do not fully understand: installed over it, 0.3.x creates entities again for 10 areas, 50 zones and 30 scenarios (including those you had not imported), cannot connect to SmartLAN/G boards, and leaves the entities only 0.4 has (such as the arming mode selects, the outputs and the diagnostic sensors) as unavailable entities. To go back to a stable version, restore that backup; this also undoes any other change made in Home Assistant since the backup.

Marketplace (2026.11 or later)HACS (2026.1 to 2026.10)Manual

On the integration's page in the Marketplace, open the menu (⋮) and choose Include pre-releases to be offered pre-releases, or Install another version and pick the version.

Turn on the repository's Pre-release switch (it is disabled by default: enable it first), or use Redownload on the integration's page and pick the version.

Download the inim_smartliving_alarm folder from the pre-release on GitHub.

Please report problems with a preview or a beta with the Beta report form, which asks for your panel model, firmware version and board type (SmartLAN/SI or SmartLAN/G).

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
Known limitations of this version, and what you can do about them:

  • On recent Home Assistant versions, new installations get entity IDs with the panel name twice (for example switch.home_home_area_3); existing installations keep their IDs. You can rename the entity IDs in each entity's settings.

  • The integration polls the panel (every 30 seconds by default, see the polling interval), so an alarm that starts and ends between two polls never shows as Triggered on the alarm panel entity or on the Area N Alarm sensor. The Alarm memory sensors of the area and the zone stay on afterwards and show that it happened, until the memory is reset (see Resetting the alarm memory).

  • The event log names the most common events: alarms, arming, disarming and resets, zone bypasses, scenarios, programming, valid codes and keys, and failed calls. Other events show as Unknown Action with their code. Decoding the remaining events is planned for an upcoming release.

  • Panels on firmware 5.0x or of another model that were set up with an earlier version keep running with the 1050's firmware 6 layout, so their names, zones, scenarios and event log may be wrong and their areas' delays are not shown. A repair notice says so. New setups of such panels are refused.

  • Dimmer levels are read from the panel on firmware 6 only: firmware 5.1 does not report them. On firmware 5.1 a dimmer's brightness is the last one set from Home Assistant, so a level changed at a keypad is not shown.

  • Analogue outputs are not offered. A terminal output on one of the panel's first three terminal positions cannot be switched remotely: the panel's output command cannot address those positions.

  • Support for firmware 5.1 is experimental and limited: it has not been tested on a real panel on firmware 5.1; the panel's state flags (such as programming mode) and the results of commands are assumed to work as on firmware 6; the free events that only firmware 5.1 has (free events 1 to 11) are shown as unknown events in the event log; and firmware 5.1 has no video sensors.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Options set how the integration reads your panel and what it does when you arm. You choose some of them when you add the panel, and can change all of them later.

docs.title: Initial options
docs.text:
When you add a panel, the last step asks for:

  • Polling Interval (seconds): how often Home Assistant reads the panel's state.
  • Number of Events to store in log: how many recent events the event log sensor keeps.
  • Arm Home, Arm Away, Arm Night, Arm Vacation and Disarm Scenario: which of your scenarios the alarm panel card runs for each button. An arm mode without a scenario is not offered; Disarm without a scenario fails with a message.

The setup proposes Arm Away and Disarm from what your scenarios do to the areas you import. Check the proposal and change it if you like.

How Arm Away and Disarm are proposed
  • Arm Away: an imported scenario that arms every imported area (one that arms them all in total mode first, then the lowest number).
  • Disarm: the lowest-numbered imported scenario that disarms every imported area.

What a scenario does to areas you do not import does not matter. If no scenario fits, the mode stays without a scenario. Only the scenarios you import are offered, and the mapping fields are shown only when at least one scenario is imported.

docs.title: Changing the options later
docs.text:
1. Go to Settings → Devices & services and open Inim SmartLiving Alarm.
  2. Click the gear icon (⚙) on your panel's row (on Home Assistant versions before 2026.11, Configure).

  3. Choose what to change:

    • Areas, zones, scenarios and outputs: what to import. The same step as at setup.
    • Area switches arm mode per area: the mode each area's switch arms in, if not the general one.
    • General settings: everything else, including a new PIN.

  4. Click Submit. The integration reloads with the new options.

docs.title: Areas, zones, scenarios and outputs
docs.text:
Tick what you want in Home Assistant. Unticking an area, zone, scenario or output removes its entities, together with any name or entity ID you gave them; ticking it again brings them back with their original entity IDs.

A scenario that an alarm panel mode uses cannot be unticked: choose another scenario for that mode in General settings first.

docs.title: Area switches arm mode per area
docs.text: Each area's switch arms in the mode chosen here when you turn it on. Use the default follows Area switches default arm mode in General settings. For example, set the bedrooms to Partial and leave the others at the default.

docs.title: General settings
docs.text: The step names the user code the current PIN belongs to and the areas it controls. Leave New PIN Code empty to keep the current PIN; a new PIN is checked with the panel as at setup.

docs.title: All options
docs.text:
Option Where Values Default What it does Polling Interval (seconds) setup, General settings 5 to 300 30 How often the panel's state is read. Shorter intervals show changes sooner and keep the board busier. Number of Events to store in log setup, General settings 1 to 100 50 How many recent events the event log sensor keeps in its attributes. Arm Home Scenario setup, General settings None (Do Not Assign) or an imported scenario none The scenario the alarm panel's Arm Home runs. Arm Away Scenario setup, General settings as above proposed The scenario the alarm panel's Arm Away runs. Arm Night Scenario setup, General settings as above none The scenario the alarm panel's Arm Night runs. Arm Vacation Scenario setup, General settings as above none The scenario the alarm panel's Arm Vacation runs. Disarm Scenario setup, General settings as above proposed The scenario the alarm panel's Disarm runs. Area switches default arm mode General settings Total, Partial, Instant Total The mode an area switch arms in when turned on. The arming mode select of each area offers every mode. Area switches arm mode per area its own step Use the default, Total, Partial, Instant, for each area Use the default A different mode for single areas' switches. When zones are not ready General settings Refuse, Arm anyway and warn Refuse What happens when zones are not ready at arming; see Zones not ready. New PIN Code General settings 1 to 6 digits, or empty empty A new PIN, checked with the panel. Empty keeps the current PIN.

The board's address, port, user name and password are changed with Reconfigure (see Setup).

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: This page shows how to add your panel to Home Assistant, how to change its connection details later, and how to read its configuration again after a change on the panel.

docs.title: Adding a panel
docs.text:
After installing the integration and restarting Home Assistant:

  1. Go to Settings → Devices & services.
  2. Click Add integration, search for Inim SmartLiving Alarm and select it.

  3. Choose how to find the panel:

    • Search the network lists the SmartLAN boards that answer and are not set up yet. Pick yours, and its address and port are filled in for you. The search only finds boards on the same subnet as Home Assistant.
    • SmartLAN/SI board or SmartLAN/G board: enter the details yourself. Use these when the search does not find your board.

  4. Enter the board's address, the port and your PIN, and give the panel a name. The fields are described below.

  5. Click Submit. The integration connects to the panel, checks it and reads its configuration. If the setup is refused, the message says why (see below).

  6. Choose the areas, zones, scenarios and outputs to import. Each one you tick gets its entities. What the panel shows in use is already ticked; change it if you like.

  7. Set the Initial Options: how often to read the panel, how many events to keep, and which scenarios the alarm panel card uses. See Options.

  8. Click Submit. The panel appears as a device with its entities: see Entities.

docs.title: Connection fields
docs.text: Field Needed for What to enter Host both boards The board's IP address, for example 192.168.1.100. Port both boards The board's TCP port: 5004 unless it was changed in the board's settings. Board user name and Board password SmartLAN/G only The user name and password of the board's web page. The board encrypts the connection with them. PIN Code both boards A user PIN of the panel, 1 to 6 digits. Commands are sent with it, so it needs the areas you want to control. Panel Name optional The name of the panel in Home Assistant, for example Home. Entity IDs start with it.

docs.title: What the items step lists
docs.text:
Areas, zones, scenarios, outputs and devices
  • Areas: every area of the panel (5 on a SmartLiving 505 or 515, 10 on a 1050, 15 on a 10100).
  • Zones: the zones of the panel. Only terminals programmed as zones are listed (outputs and unused terminals are not), including the second zones of double terminals (11 to 20 on the 505, 21 to 40 on the 515, 51 to 100 on the 1050, 101 to 200 on the 10100).
  • Scenarios: every scenario of the panel (30).
  • Outputs: the outputs your user code may switch, with their kind (on/off, monostable with its time, or dimmer); the section is shown only if there are some. Only the outputs the installer marked as home automation outputs are ticked (firmware 6): an output can drive a siren, a lock or a gate, so tick only the ones you mean to switch from Home Assistant (see Outputs).
  • Found on the panel: the keypads, readers, expanders and sirens enabled on the panel, by name, for reference.

The setup ticks what the panel shows in use: the zones that belong to an area, the areas of those zones, the scenarios that change at least one area, and the outputs the installer marked as home automation outputs. Each section can be folded.

docs.title: Why the setup can be refused
docs.text: Message What to do Failed to connect. Please check the Host and Port … Check the address and port, that Home Assistant can reach the board, and that no other program is connected to it (see Troubleshooting). The PIN must be 1 to 6 digits. Enter the PIN as digits only. The PIN does not match any user code of the panel. Enter the PIN of a user code programmed on the panel. The SmartLAN/G board did not accept the connection. Check the board's user name and password. The SmartLAN/G board answered, but its reply was not in the expected format. If the user name and password are right, your board may answer in a way the integration does not handle yet: see Troubleshooting. The panel is in programming mode … Try again when programming has ended. The panel's firmware is not supported: firmware 5.1 or newer is needed. Firmware older than 5.1 cannot be set up. This SmartLiving model is not supported yet. Please report the model and firmware on GitHub. This Inim Alarm panel is already configured. The panel is already set up in Home Assistant.

docs.title: Changing the connection details (Reconfigure)
docs.text:
If the address, port or PIN of your panel change (or, for SmartLAN/G, the board's user name or password), you do not need to remove and add the integration again:

  1. Go to Settings → Devices & services and open Inim SmartLiving Alarm.
  2. Open the menu (⋮) of your panel's entry and choose Reconfigure.
  3. Enter the new details and click Submit. The PIN and the board password are not filled in: leave them empty to keep the current ones.

The integration contacts the panel with the new details, reads its configuration again and reloads. Your options, entities and entity IDs are kept.

What Reconfigure checks
  • If the panel cannot be reached, an error is shown and nothing is changed.
  • An address already used by another configured panel is refused, and so is a PIN that does not match any user code of the panel.
  • The board type (SmartLAN/SI or SmartLAN/G) cannot be changed here: remove the integration and add it again for that.

docs.title: Re-reading the panel configuration
docs.text:
The integration reads the panel's names and programming when you add it: the names of areas, zones, scenarios, user codes, keys, keypads, readers, expanders, timers and sirens; which keypads, readers, expanders and sirens are enabled; the zone setup and the scenario definitions. If you change them on the panel later (from a keypad or the installer software), read them again with either:

  • the Re-read panel configuration button, in the Configuration section of your panel's device page, or
  • the Re-read panel configuration action, inim_smartliving_alarm.reread_panel_configuration (see Actions).

The integration then reloads with the new configuration.

What changes after a re-read
  • Your options are not changed, and entity IDs stay the same; entity names follow the new names from the panel.
  • The areas, zones and scenarios you import are not changed either: a zone wired later or a new scenario is listed, unticked, in the options under Areas, zones, scenarios and outputs.
  • If the panel cannot be reached, or it is in programming mode, an error is shown and the stored configuration is kept: in programming mode, try again when programming has ended.

docs.title: System report
docs.text: When you report a problem, a system report tells what the integration knows about your panel: model and firmware, board, the panel's programming as read from it, status, the event log, the integration's options and entities, and connection statistics.

docs.title: Sharing a report
docs.text:
1. Open your panel's device page: Settings → Devices & services → Inim SmartLiving Alarm → your panel.

  2. Click Download diagnostics in the Device info card.

  3. Wait for the file: it takes about 40 seconds on SmartLAN/SI. Commands are not held up meanwhile.

  4. Attach the file to your GitHub issue. If GitHub refuses the file, zip it first.

The same entry is in the menu (⋮) of your panel on the integration's page.

docs.title: How much the report shows
docs.text:
The Diagnostics level select chooses how much the next report shows. It is disabled by default: enable it on the device page, in the Diagnostic section.

Level What it contains Redacted (default) Everything public: the programming, status, events with their times, statistics. Names are cut to their first 3 characters, the serial number to its last 4 digits, the board's MAC address to its last 2 bytes; addresses, PINs, phone numbers, key serials and passwords are left out. Safe to post. Full Also the names, the serial number and the network addresses. PINs, phone numbers, key serials and passwords are still left out. Full confidential Everything, including the PINs, phone numbers, key serials and the board's passwords.

At Redacted, one download gives a plain file you can attach to a GitHub issue as it is.

Full and Full confidential: two files

At Full and Full confidential you get two files from the same reading of the panel:

  1. The first download is encrypted to the maintainer's key: only the matching private key decrypts it. It also holds the Redacted view in clear. Attach this file to your GitHub issue; it is the only file to share.
  2. Download diagnostics once more within 10 minutes to get a readable copy of the same report (it holds PRIVATE COPY), to check what you are sharing. Do not share it: keep it private and delete it when you no longer need it. A notification reminds you of this after the first download. Both files get the same name, so your browser saves the second one with a number added (for example (1)): attach the first one, which holds encrypted and redacted_view, never the one that holds PRIVATE COPY.

Then the level goes back to Redacted. Nothing is stored: the report is held in memory only until the second download, for 10 minutes at most.

What is and is not read

The board's own details (its network settings and firmware) are included only when Home Assistant is on the same network as the board. What is never read, at any level: the panel's cloud keys, account ID and address, and the board's internal keys.

docs.title: Reading a report
docs.text:
The repository has a small viewer for reports, scripts/inim_report.py (Python 3.13 or newer; nothing to install for reading). Download the repository from GitHub, then:

  • python3 scripts/inim_report.py show REPORT.json shows a report: a summary and the findings first, then areas, zones, scenarios, codes, devices, outputs, the areas' state now, status, events, the integration's options and the connection. Add --html report.html for one page to open in a browser.
  • python3 scripts/inim_report.py check REPORT.json says whether a file is the one to attach (the Redacted report, or the encrypted one) or the private copy, which you should not share.

An encrypted report is read with show REPORT.json --decrypt (add --html report.html for the page); it needs the matching private key and the Python package cryptography. It reads the files only: it connects to nothing. You can view your own Redacted report and your readable copy with it; the encrypted file shows its Redacted view.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Start with the table: find your problem, then follow the link for the details.

Problem What to check The setup is refused The message on the form: see Why the setup can be refused. Home Assistant cannot connect Address, port, network, firewall: see Cannot connect. Search the network finds no board Same subnet, free UDP ports: see Search finds no board. A command fails with a message The message says why: see When the panel refuses a command. Arming is refused because zones are not ready Close or bypass the zones, or arm anyway: see Zones not ready. Commands fail with "the panel is in programming mode" Wait until programming has ended: see Programming mode. Names, zones or scenarios are out of date Use Re-read panel configuration: see Setup. Entities are missing, too many, or not updating See Entities missing or not updating. The Inim app cannot connect locally See The Inim app. Reporting a problem Attach a system report to the GitHub issue, and if you can a debug log.

docs.title: When the panel refuses a command
docs.text:
Arming, disarming, bypassing a zone, running a scenario, resetting the alarm memory and switching an output fail with a message when they are not carried out. The message says which of three things happened.

1. The integration did not send the command.

  • Before arming or running a scenario, the integration checks the zones (see Zones not ready). If some are not ready and the option says Refuse, the message lists them and nothing is sent to the panel.
  • While the panel is in programming mode, it ignores commands, so none is sent ("The command for Area 3 was not sent: the panel is in programming mode. Try again when programming has ended."). If the panel enters programming mode while a command is being sent, the message says that the command may not have been carried out: check the area or zone, and try again when programming has ended.

2. The panel refused it. The message gives the panel's reason:

Message Reason in events What to do The panel did not accept the PIN invalid_code The user code was changed or deleted on the panel: enter the current PIN with Reconfigure. The PIN is not enabled for it code_not_enabled The user code does not control that area: enable it on the panel or use another code. It does not allow arming while zones are not ready open_zones Close or bypass the open zones of the area, then arm again. The zone cannot be bypassed cannot_be_bypassed The zone's programming on the panel does not allow it. The zone belongs to no area no_areas The zone's programming on the panel does not allow it. Double zone error double_zone_error The zone's programming on the panel does not allow it. It is already in the requested state already_in_state Nothing to do: the zone or area was already as requested. Its terminal is out of range slot_out_of_range The zone's or output's terminal has changed on the panel: use Re-read panel configuration. Its terminal is not connected slot_not_connected As above. Its terminal is not in use null_terminal As above. The output is not enabled output_not_enabled Your user code may not switch that output: enable it for the code on the panel, or untick the output. The output is locked while its areas are armed areas_armed The panel does not let the output change while its areas are armed: disarm them first. The panel refused the command refused The panel gave no reason. The panel refused the command (result code N) unknown The panel gave a reason the integration does not know yet.

3. The command could not be completed. The panel could not be reached, or its answer could not be read. See Cannot connect; try again once the connection is back.

A failed scenario also shows a notification and fires the inim_smartliving_alarm_scenario_activation_failed event, with the reason.

docs.title: Cannot connect
docs.text:
• Verify the IP address and port of your SmartLAN board.
  • Make sure Home Assistant can reach the board's address on that port (check firewalls and network segmentation).
  • Make sure the board is powered and connected to the network.
  • If the board's address or port has changed, update it with Reconfigure (see Changing the connection details) instead of removing the integration.

docs.title: Search finds no board
docs.text:
• The search only reaches boards on the same subnet as Home Assistant (the boards answer only on their own network segment). Enter a board on another subnet or VLAN by hand.
  • The search listens on UDP ports 5001 (SmartLAN/SI) and 7001 (SmartLAN/G) of the Home Assistant host; another program using them, or a firewall, prevents it.
  • Boards that are already set up are not listed.

docs.title: SmartLAN/G: the reply was not in the expected format
docs.text: The setup says "The SmartLAN/G board answered, but its reply was not in the expected format". Check the board's user name and password first. If they are right, your board probably answers in a way this integration does not handle yet. Please open a GitHub issue with your panel model and firmware, the board's version and a debug log of a setup attempt.

docs.title: The Inim app cannot connect locally
docs.text: The SmartLAN/SI board accepts only one local connection at a time. Home Assistant keeps its connection open while it reads the panel and for a few seconds after each update, so the app may have to retry. Remote access through Inim Cloud is not affected.

docs.title: Programming mode
docs.text:
• Someone is programming the panel from a keypad, or the panel is reloading its configuration. Commands work again when programming has ended; the Programming mode sensor shows when.
  • Programming from the installer software on a PC does not block commands. After the software writes new programming, the panel may restart by itself, and Home Assistant cannot reach it for a short time. Then use Re-read panel configuration to pick up the changes.

docs.title: Commands not carried out
docs.text:
• The error message tells why (see When the panel refuses a command).
  • Check that the PIN is a valid user PIN of the panel, with the areas you want to control. Setup and Reconfigure refuse a PIN that matches no user code; for a panel set up with an older version of the integration, the log shows a warning ("The PIN does not match any user code of the panel") each time the integration connects. Change it with Reconfigure (see Changing the connection details).
  • Arming is refused because zones are not ready: close or bypass the zones the message lists, or set When zones are not ready to Arm anyway and warn (or use force: true in an action). See Zones not ready.

docs.title: Entities missing or not updating
docs.text:
• Check the Home Assistant logs (Settings → System → Logs) for errors from the inim_smartliving_alarm integration.
  • Check the polling interval in the options. Too short can overload the panel or the network; too long delays updates.
  • Only ticked items get entities: check the options under Areas, zones, scenarios and outputs.
  • A zone is listed only if its terminal is programmed as a zone on the panel. If you changed the panel's programming, use Re-read panel configuration first.
Rare cases: no switches, no scenario buttons

The area, zone and output switches are created only when the panel data stored for the areas has names, and the scenario buttons only when the scenarios have names. If they are all missing, use Re-read panel configuration; the log says when the names are missing.

docs.title: Debug log
docs.text:
To get a debug log, add this to configuration.yaml, restart Home Assistant and repeat what failed:

logger:
  logs:
    custom_components.inim_smartliving_alarm: debug

The log shows the requests and replies; the PIN is masked, and the board's user name and password are never logged. Remove the lines again afterwards.

docs.title: From 0.3.x
docs.text: Version 0.4 reworks how the integration talks to the panel. Your entity IDs and options stay as they are, and your configuration entry is updated automatically.

docs.title: Before you update
docs.text:
1. Take a Home Assistant backup (Settings → System → Backups), above all for a preview or a beta (see Preview versions).
  2. Read the changes below, above all those marked check your automations.

docs.title: After you update
docs.text:
1. Look at the log after the first start. The integration may read the panel configuration again by itself, once, and says so.
  2. Delete leftover entities: entities of terminals that are not zones, or of zones and areas your panel does not have, stay as unavailable entities and are listed in the log at every start. Delete them in Settings → Devices & services → Entities.
  3. Tick what is new in the options under Areas, zones, scenarios and outputs: the second zones of double terminals, areas 11 to 15 and zones above 50 on a 10100, and outputs.
  4. Choose what happens with zones not ready: arming now checks the zones, and refuses by default (see Zones not ready).
  5. Check your automations and templates against the changes marked check your automations.

docs.title: Areas and the alarm panel
docs.text:
Change What to do Area switches are on for partial and instant arming too Check your automations if they relied on the switch being off then Area X Triggered is now Area X Alarm memory; new Area X Alarm and Area X Tamper sensors Nothing: same entity ID The alarm panel shows Triggered only while an area is in alarm Check your automations: use the Alarm memory sensors for the memory New arming mode select per area, and the arm_area action Add them to dashboards and automations if you like Each area switch can arm in its own mode Optional: Area switches arm mode per area Each area's delays are shown as attributes Nothing Details
  • Area switches are now on for an area armed in partial or instant mode too (before, such an area showed as unknown and its switch was off). Turning a switch on still arms in total mode, unless you choose another mode with the new Area switches default arm mode option. The new arming_mode attribute tells the mode (total, partial, instant or disarmed); status_text stays armed or disarmed.
  • "Area X Triggered" is now called "Area X Alarm memory": same entity ID, same meaning (on after an alarm until the memory is reset), now also for areas 9 and 10, with a tamper_memory attribute. Two new binary sensors per area show the live state: Area X Alarm and Area X Tamper.
  • The alarm panel shows Triggered only while an area is in alarm. Before, it stayed Triggered until the alarm memory was reset; now it returns to its armed or disarmed state when the alarm ends, and the Alarm memory sensors keep the memory. Automations that relied on Triggered lasting until the reset should use the Alarm memory sensors instead.
  • New: an arming mode select per area (Area X arming mode: disarmed, total, partial or instant) and the arm_area action, which arms or disarms several areas in one command (see Arming areas from automations).
  • Each area switch can arm in its own mode: the new options step Area switches arm mode per area has one choice per imported area (use the default, total, partial or instant). Areas left at Use the default follow Area switches default arm mode, as before. The general option, called Area switches arm in in the 0.4.0a3 preview, is now Area switches default arm mode: if you changed it in that preview, set it again (it is back to total).
  • Each area's delays are shown: the Area X arming mode select's attributes now include the area's exit and entry times, entry time 2, pre-arm warning and patrol times, timer program and three options, read from the panel. At the first start the integration reads the panel configuration again once by itself to get them (the log says so); if it cannot, they appear after the next start or a Re-read panel configuration.

docs.title: Zones
docs.text:
Change What to do Zones follow the panel's terminal types; second zones of double terminals can be added Delete leftover entities; tick second zones if you want them Zone X Triggered is now Zone X Alarm memory; new Zone X Tamper sensor Nothing: same entity ID Zones are checked before arming areas too, and arming is refused by default Choose When zones are not ready Zone attributes show the real programming; some are renamed Check your automations and templates Zone device classes follow the zone's programming Set Show as on a zone to keep its old class Details
  • Zones follow the panel's terminal types. Output terminals (for example a siren) and unused terminals no longer get zone entities, and the second zones of double terminals (11 to 20 on the 505, 21 to 40 on the 515, 51 to 100 on the 1050, 101 to 200 on the 10100) can be added: tick them in the options under Areas, zones, scenarios and outputs (existing installations keep the zones they had). Entities that earlier versions created for terminals that are not zones are not deleted automatically: they stay as unavailable entities, and the log lists them at every start ("these entities belong to terminals that are not zones on the panel"). Delete them in Settings → Devices & services → Entities.
  • "Zone X Triggered" is now called "Zone X Alarm memory" (same entity ID). Zones in short circuit or tamper are no longer shown as unknown: a new Zone X Tamper sensor turns on, and the zone's status_text says short or tamper. Such zones are also listed when they prevent a scenario from being activated.
  • Zones are checked before arming areas too. The area switches, the arming mode selects and the arm_area action now ask the panel which zones are not ready, as scenarios already did, and by default refuse to arm when there are some (before, they armed with zones open). The new option When zones are not ready (General settings) can arm anyway with a warning instead; force: true does it for one action call. A new action, activate_scenario, activates a scenario from automations, and a new event, inim_smartliving_alarm_zones_not_ready, lists the zones each time. The integration also reads whether the panel itself refuses arming with zones not ready (new diagnostic sensor Refuses arming with zones not ready): at the first start it reads the panel configuration again once by itself (the log says so). Zone sensors show each zone's programming options (autobypass, no_arming_if_not_ready, interior and more) as attributes.
  • Zone attributes now show the zone's real programming, read from the panel configuration already stored (nothing is read again). Before, most zone types and balancings showed as Unknown, and two times were read wrongly. Some attributes are renamed, so check templates and automations that use them: activation_type is now zone_type, balancing_type is balancing, sensor_type is sensor_kind, duration_ms is now alarm_pulse_duration (or shock_sensitivity for shock sensors), time is pulse_window_time and pulses is pulse_count. New: alarm_cycles. Values are now lower-case English keys (for example delayed, double_eol, input instead of Delayed, Double Balancing, Input).
  • Zone device classes follow the zone's programming. Single EOL zones are now opening (before, no class), shock sensors are vibration (before, opening or none), and roller-blind sensors are opening (before, motion). Normally open, normally closed and double EOL zones keep their class. To keep the old class on a zone, set it with Show as in the entity's settings.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
Change What to do New setups propose the Arm Away and Disarm scenarios Nothing: existing installations keep their mappings Scenarios that arm partially or instantly are read correctly Check your automations that use area_actions_details A scenario stopped by zones not ready lists the zones the panel reported Nothing Details
  • New setups propose the Arm Away and Disarm scenarios from what your scenarios do to the areas you import. Existing installations keep their mappings.
  • Scenarios that arm partially or instantly are read correctly. The area_actions_details attribute of the scenario buttons now says total, partial or instant for the areas a scenario arms (before, arm for total and unknown for the other two). A scenario that disarms some areas and arms others partially or instantly was treated as a disarm scenario, so if the panel refused it, the message did not list the zones that blocked it; now it does.
  • A scenario stopped by zones not ready lists the zones the panel reported. The persistent notification and the blocking_zones of the inim_smartliving_alarm_scenario_activation_failed event now list the same zones as the error message, including zones at rest that the panel counts as not ready (delayed zones, for example), each with status not_ready. Before, they listed only the zones in alarm or tamper, and could say that no zones were found.

docs.title: Commands and errors
docs.text:
Change What to do Commands that are not carried out now show an error Check your automations: a failed step stops them unless it has continue_on_error: true Programming mode is detected; no command is sent then Nothing Details
  • Commands that are not carried out now show an error. Before, a refused arm, disarm, bypass or reset was only written to the log, and the alarm panel's error notifications did not appear at all. Now the action fails with a message that tells why (for example a PIN the panel no longer accepts, or a PIN not enabled for that area), in the dashboard and in automation traces; see When the panel refuses a command. An automation step that fails stops that automation unless the step has continue_on_error: true. The inim_smartliving_alarm_scenario_activation_failed event has a new panel_result field (the panel's answer, or null when the panel did not refuse the command), and its reason can now also be command_failed or invalid_code.
  • Programming mode is now detected. While the panel is being programmed from a keypad, it ignores commands, and earlier versions reported such a command as carried out. Now no command is sent while the panel is in programming mode: the action fails with a message instead, and setup, Reconfigure and Re-read panel configuration are refused with a message: try again when programming has ended. A new diagnostic sensor, Programming mode, shows it. The reason of the inim_smartliving_alarm_scenario_activation_failed event can now also be panel_programming.

docs.title: Event log and names
docs.text:
Change What to do Event times are in Home Assistant's time zone; the state is the event's position in the log Check your automations that use the state's value The event log shows the names programmed on the panel; the Reader names option is removed Nothing: the names come from the panel Names with accented letters show them in full Nothing Details
  • Event log: event times are now shown in Home Assistant's time zone, with daylight saving time (before, always UTC+1), and new events keep appearing after the panel's event log wraps around. The event log sensor's state is now the newest event's position in the panel's log (0 to 999, or 0 to 499 on panels that keep 500 events: the SmartLiving 505 and 515, and the 1050 on firmware 5.1) instead of a memory address: automations that only trigger on a change keep working, but compare the new numbers if you used the value itself.
  • The event log shows the names programmed on the panel: who caused an event (the user code's or key's name, instead of User 3 or Key 5) and where (the keypad's or reader's name). Commands sent remotely, from the app, the cloud, Home Assistant or the installer software, show Remote (before, Mobile App). The Reader names option is removed: reader names now come from the panel, and names typed in that option are no longer used. Your configuration entry is updated once more (version 1.5), and at the first start the integration reads the panel configuration again by itself to get the names (the log says so). A new diagnostic sensor, Peripherals, lists the keypads, readers, expanders and sirens enabled on the panel, and so does the Areas, zones, scenarios and outputs step.
  • Names with accented letters now show them in full. Area, zone, scenario and keypad names programmed with letters such as à, è, é or ù lost them before; they are now read with the panel's own character set, like the names of user codes, keys and other devices. The names come from the panel data already stored, so nothing is read again. Entity IDs do not change, and names you changed in Home Assistant stay as you set them.

docs.title: Setup, options and connection
docs.text:
Change What to do One connection to the panel, reused Nothing; see the Inim app New: SmartLAN/G boards, a network search, all areas of your user code in the active scenario Nothing The PIN is checked when you Reconfigure; changing it in the options works again Nothing You pick the areas, zones and scenarios from lists; unticking removes entities Nothing: your counts became the same items SmartLAN/G replies are read correctly Nothing Details
  • Your configuration entry is updated automatically (it is marked as a SmartLAN/SI connection). Entity IDs and options do not change.
  • Home Assistant now keeps one connection to the panel and reuses it, so updates are faster. The SmartLAN/SI board accepts only one local connection: see the Inim app under Troubleshooting.
  • The PIN is checked from now on when you Reconfigure: a PIN that matches no user code of the panel is refused. If your current PIN matches none, the log shows a warning at every connection.
  • New: SmartLAN/G boards, a network search when adding a panel, and the active scenario now takes all areas of your user code into account (previously areas 8 to 10 were ignored).
  • Your configuration entry is updated once more (version 1.3): the zone list is completed from the panel data already stored, without contacting the panel. If that data is incomplete, a warning asks you to use Re-read panel configuration.
  • SmartLAN/G: the board's replies are now read the way the board sends them (the data alone, without the panel's checksum). Before, every read failed and setup reported a wrong user name or password even with the right credentials. A wrong user name or password is now reported only when the board's reply cannot be decrypted; any other unexpected reply has its own message (see Troubleshooting).
  • You now pick the areas, zones and scenarios to import from lists, by name, instead of giving how many of each. Your configuration entry is updated once more (version 1.4): the counts you had become the same items (for example, 7 areas become areas 1 to 7), so your entities do not change. A scenario used by an alarm panel mode beyond your scenario count is added, so that the mode keeps working. The options now open a menu: Areas, zones, scenarios and outputs or General settings. Unticking an item there removes its entities; ticking it again brings them back with the same entity IDs. Entities left over from areas, zones or scenarios above your old counts are removed at the first start.
  • The arm_area action lists the imported areas only, by name, and refuses areas that are not imported. The alarm panel's modes can be mapped only to imported scenarios.
  • Changing the PIN in the options works again, and the PIN is no longer shown. The New PIN Code field in General settings is now empty: leave it empty to keep the current PIN, or enter a new one, which is checked with the panel as at setup. Before, the field showed the current PIN in clear text and any new PIN was refused. The PIN (and, for SmartLAN/G, the board password) is now a password field at setup and in Reconfigure, where it is no longer filled in: leave it empty to keep the current one. A new diagnostic sensor, User code, names the user code the PIN belongs to, and General settings says it too.
  • More of the integration is translated. The notifications (a scenario blocked or failed, an area armed with zones not ready), the scenario choices of the alarm panel's modes in the options, and the names and fields of the actions now follow Home Assistant's language (English or Italian). The message of the inim_smartliving_alarm_scenario_activation_failed event stays in English. The alarm_reset action on a panel whose integration is not loaded now fails with a message, instead of doing nothing.

docs.title: Panels and firmware
docs.text:
Change What to do SmartLiving 10100, 505 and 515 use their own memory layout Look at the log; delete leftover entities; tick new areas and zones Firmware 5.1 panels use their own layout (experimental) Look at the log Firmware 5.0x and other models cannot be set up any more Existing setups keep working, with a repair notice Details
  • SmartLiving 10100 (experimental on firmware 5.1): a 10100 now uses its own memory layout. Earlier versions read it as if it were a 1050, so its names and zones were wrong: at the first start after the update the integration reads the panel configuration again by itself (the log says so). Entity IDs of areas and zones stay the same; areas 11 to 15 and zones above 50 can be ticked in the options under Areas, zones, scenarios and outputs.
  • SmartLiving 505 and 515 (experimental): they now use their own memory layout. Earlier versions read them as if they were a 1050, so their names, zones, scenarios and event log were wrong. At the first start after the update the integration reads the panel configuration again by itself (the log says so). Entity IDs stay the same; zones and areas the panel does not have stay as unavailable entities and are listed in the log, as for the 10100: delete them in Settings → Devices & services → Entities. Please report how it works.
  • Firmware 5.1 (experimental): panels on firmware 5.1 now use their own memory layout. Earlier versions read them as if they were a 1050 on firmware 6, so their names, zones, scenarios and event log were wrong. At the first start after the update the integration reads the panel configuration again by itself (the log says so), and the "panel not supported" repair notice goes away. Event log descriptions are now right on these panels. See the limits of firmware 5.1 support. Please report how it works.
  • Firmware 5.0x and other models cannot be set up any more: a new setup of a panel on firmware older than 5.1, or of a SmartLiving model without its own layout, is refused with a message. A panel of such a model, or one on firmware 5.0x, that is already set up keeps working as before and shows a repair notice, as its data may be wrong.

docs.title: New features
docs.text:
Change What to do Outputs can be switched and dimmed Tick them in the options System reports See System report The integration has its own icon Shown on Home Assistant 2026.3 or later Details
  • Outputs are new: terminal outputs and the fixed outputs O1 to O3 can be switched, and dimmers dimmed, from Home Assistant. At the first start the integration reads the panel configuration again once by itself to get the outputs' programming and names (the log says so). No output is imported until you save the options under Areas, zones, scenarios and outputs, where the outputs the installer marked as home automation outputs are ticked for you.
  • System reports are new: downloading the integration's diagnostics now gives a system report for bug reports, at the level chosen with the new Diagnostics level select (disabled by default). See Sharing a system report.
  • The integration has its own icon, shown on Home Assistant 2026.3 or later; earlier versions show none, as before.

Limits of this version: see Known limitations.
